title: A year within reach
method: 25 statute miles = 40.2336 km, great-circle (haversine), Earth radius 6,371.0088 km. The on-screen local equirectangular projection uses the center latitude; the boundary is sampled geodesically. Neighborhood shapes and coastline are schematic editorial illustrations, not GIS boundaries or measured weather interpolation.

seasons.name: Winter
seasons.title: Make room for rain.
seasons.summary: Most rainfall arrives in the cool half of the year. Plan an outdoor window, a dry return and an indoor alternative. A wet year and a dry year can have very different rhythms.
seasons.outdoor: Choose a dry daylight interval and paved routes after rain; check closures, surf and NWS warnings before leaving.
seasons.comfort: Keep a removable layer near the door. Cool evenings can matter even when the afternoon feels mild.
seasons.home: Repair drafts and leaks; ventilate briefly when outdoor air is clean and conditions allow. Keep runoff paths clear.
seasons.water: Pause irrigation after meaningful rain according to your site and local rules; dry winters still require care.

seasons.name: Spring
seasons.title: Follow the light, keep a layer.
seasons.summary: Rain tapers while the marine layer becomes a familiar coastal visitor. Overcast does not promise cool conditions everywhere: a few miles inland or an exposed slope can tell another story.
seasons.outdoor: Try a late-morning coastal outing if low cloud persists; choose shade when inland sun arrives. Check the actual cloud and wind first.
seasons.comfort: Pack one light layer instead of betting on the first look outside. Wind and exposure change comfort.
seasons.home: Use a simple indoor/outdoor temperature check before opening windows. Air quality and noise also count.
seasons.water: Review soil moisture and plant needs before adding summer irrigation; use mulch and repair drips.

seasons.name: Summer
seasons.title: Bring shade into the plan.
seasons.summary: Rain is normally scarce; inland afternoons are warmer than the immediate coast. Morning low cloud may offer a gentler start, but coastal cooling can fail during heat events.
seasons.outdoor: Favor earlier or later outdoor time, shade and access to water; check heat alerts. Comfort is individual and cloud cover is variable.
seasons.comfort: Shade sun-facing windows before heat accumulates. A timer can remind you to stop and recheck conditions.
seasons.home: Ventilate only when outside is cooler and air is clean; during smoke use official AirNow guidance. A window cue is not an air-quality sensor.
seasons.water: Use local watering rules, efficient irrigation and drought-tolerant planting. The normal dry season is not a drought declaration.

seasons.name: Autumn
seasons.title: Expect the season to turn twice.
seasons.summary: Early autumn can remain hot. Offshore Santa Ana episodes can bring warm, dry, gusty air; later autumn begins the transition toward rain. Smoke can occur in any season.
seasons.outdoor: Check heat, fire-weather, wind and smoke notices before an exposed walk. Swap the plan for a sheltered indoor activity when conditions worsen.
seasons.comfort: Keep shade gear ready in September, then restore the rain kit as winter approaches. Calendar dates do not define the weather.
seasons.home: Keep a clean-air room plan and check filters. Shut windows during smoke; follow AirNow and local official instructions.
seasons.water: Inspect gutters and runoff before the first storm; keep water conservation habits through warm spells.

zones.name: Ocean edge
zones.places: El Segundo · Manhattan Beach · Santa Monica
zones.pattern: Cooler typical summer afternoons, onshore breeze, low cloud and salt exposure. Marine influence varies by day and distance from the water.
zones.evidence: LAX is the main numeric coastal anchor here. Beaches, street canyons and bluffs are not measured by the airport thermometer.

advice.outdoor: Start with a layered coastal walk; use wind, cloud and current heat conditions to choose the hour.
advice.comfort: Carry a light layer for breeze and shade for any sunny interval.
advice.home: A clean, cooler sea breeze can help; a closed window is often better when smoke, traffic air or noise is present.
advice.water: Salt and wind affect planting and gear. Rinse and repair objects; irrigate for soil need, not the map color.

zones.name: Inland basin
zones.pattern: Less direct ocean cooling and more warm surfaces. Inland afternoon heat often rises faster than at the beach; tree cover and buildings vary block by block.
zones.evidence: Downtown's NOAA composite series provides a contrast, not a neighborhood temperature surface. Station location has changed.

advice.outdoor: Choose shade and an earlier or later outing; check heat advisories even if the coastal forecast looks mild.
advice.comfort: Sun exposure, pavement and humidity matter beyond air temperature. Put shade and a refill stop in the route.
advice.home: Shade first; compare indoor/outdoor temperatures before ventilating. Keep an indoor alternative for heat and smoke.
advice.water: Use mulch, fix leaks and follow local rules. Hot pavement is not proof that a plant needs water.

zones.name: South Bay & port plain
zones.pattern: A transition from coastal breeze to warmer inland airport and industrial plain settings. Terrain and distance from the water alter afternoon wind.
zones.evidence: Long Beach airport supplies a southern/inland reference. It does not characterize every coastal block or port exposure.

advice.outdoor: Check the local wind and heat, then choose shade; airport normals do not set waterfront comfort.
advice.comfort: A simple shaded rest and refill plan is useful before a long outing.
advice.home: Check air quality near your actual location; this atlas does not map pollution or emissions.
advice.water: Keep a rain-ready kit and efficient irrigation plan for the long dry season.

zones.name: Hills & exposed slopes
zones.places: Palos Verdes · Santa Monica foothills (inside circle)
zones.pattern: Elevation, slope, aspect and exposure add contrast. Some slopes may sit above a shallow marine layer; wind and fire weather can matter more than the seasonal mean.
zones.evidence: No dedicated hill normal is used in this edition. This is a qualitative terrain class; no lapse-rate correction or precise contour is claimed.

advice.outdoor: Check trail closures and wind. Choose a shaded route with an easy return; avoid treating a hill as automatic heat relief.
advice.comfort: Bring a layer for exposure and shade for sun. Coastal low cloud can lie below an exposed hillside.
advice.home: Terrain can amplify wind. Use current local alerts, not this map, for operational decisions.
advice.water: Slope and runoff matter. Inspect drainage before rain and follow local drought and fire guidance.

zones.name: Northern inland edge
zones.pattern: Within the circle's northern reach, summer afternoons are typically warmer and winter nights cooler than at LAX. Valley topography can shelter or channel wind.
zones.evidence: Burbank airport is one measured anchor near the radius edge; nearby mountain sectors remain poorly represented.

advice.outdoor: Treat heat planning as a first step: shade, a shorter route and current alerts.
advice.comfort: A larger day-to-night swing can make a layer useful after an early or late outing.
advice.home: Consider cooler-night ventilation only with clean outdoor air and a safe window setup.
advice.water: Conserve through the dry season; prepare for episodic rain rather than expecting evenly spread rainfall.

sources.title: NOAA U.S. Climate Normals / periods, quality and comparison method
sources.use: Defines station normals, available-year flags and consistent-version comparison cautions. Four raw monthly station CSVs are linked above and downloadable below.

sources.title: NWS Downtown Los Angeles observing-site move notice
sources.use: Series began July 1877; Civic Center 1964–1999, USC since 1999, relocation in May 2024. Moves limit direct site comparisons.

sources.title: NOAA Historical Observing Metadata Repository
sources.use: Station coordinates, elevations and histories. The historical USC anchor differs from coordinates retained in the monthly normals CSV.

sources.title: NOAA GHCN-Daily station data and quality flags
sources.use: Daily records were aggregated for complete calendar years 1991–2025 at LAX and Downtown. Nonmissing values with blank quality flag only; trace measured rain retained as zero. Daily file links are included in downloads.

sources.title: NOAA JetStream: Marine Layer
sources.use: Explains inversion, variable depth, terrain reach and May Gray / June Gloom. Does not establish cloud hours on any atlas parcel.

sources.title: NWS Los Angeles: Weather of Southern California, WR-261 (2000)
sources.use: Historic regional interpretation: station-location map, August 1999 inversion and wind maps. Historic statistics and service guidance are not used as current warnings.

sources.title: NWS Mountain and Valley Winds
sources.use: Santa Ana mechanism and September–May occurrence context. Offshore-wind checks apply beyond autumn.

sources.title: NOAA California State Climate Summary 2022
sources.use: Observations through 2020 show nearly 3°F statewide warming since the early twentieth century and major rainfall variability. State trend context and future emissions scenarios are separate from local station evidence.

sources.title: NOAA/WPC Daily Weather Map archive
sources.use: Dated synoptic charts and historical 1871–2002 scans; these are weather snapshots, not porch-scale climatology.

sources.title: USGS Historical Topographic Maps
sources.use: Preserves printed map editions from 1884–2006. Contours explain landscape; elevation lines are not measured weather boundaries.

sources.title: PRISM 1991–2020 normals
sources.use: 800 m and 4 km modeled climate grids. Linked as a future quantitative mapping option; no PRISM raster was processed for this edition.

sources.title: PRISM mapping methods
sources.use: Models consider terrain, station information and coastal influence; modeled cell values still need uncertainty and validation.

sources.title: NWS During a Heat Wave
sources.use: Basis for cooler activity periods, shade breaks and an indoor cooling alternative. Seasonal mean is not a heat-alert threshold.

sources.title: EPA Wildfires and Indoor Air Quality
sources.use: Explains smoke entering homes and the limits of ventilation. Use current AirNow and official guidance.

sources.title: EPA Create a Clean Room
sources.use: Source for clean-air room planning, commercial filtration and cooling tradeoffs. No library object is an air cleaner.

sources.title: NOAA NIDIS California drought information
sources.use: Dated drought context and different water-system impacts. A normal dry season is not a drought declaration.

sources.title: NWS Flood Safety
sources.use: Current storm guidance overrides seasonal route ideas. The atlas does not estimate route passability.

sources.title: Nouns visual culture
sources.use: Inspiration for original square-glasses illustrations. No Nouns token assets or code imported. Independent art; no official Nouns affiliation.

stations.name: LAX · coast
stations.quality: NOAA variable-specific flags: High (TMAX): S, 26–27 available years; Low (TMIN): S, 27–29 available years; Mean (TAVG): S, 26–27 available years; Rain: S, 30–30 years. S = Standard; R = Representative. Missing months may be estimated.
stations.history: Airport metadata reaches 1930; supplied daily elements begin August 1944. Airport exposure is a coastal reference, not a beach or home measurement.

stations.name: Downtown / USC · historical series
stations.quality: NOAA variable-specific flags: High (TMAX): S, 26–28 available years; Low (TMIN): S, 25–27 available years; Mean (TAVG): R/S, 25–27 available years; Rain: S, 30–30 years. S = Standard; R = Representative. Missing months may be estimated.
stations.history: Downtown climate series began in 1877. Civic Center observations moved to USC in 1999 and to FHMC in 2024. Normal is a composite historical series.

stations.name: Burbank airport · inland valley
stations.quality: NOAA variable-specific flags: High (TMAX): R, 20–21 available years; Low (TMIN): R, 18–20 available years; Mean (TAVG): R, 18–20 available years; Rain: R, 20–23 years. S = Standard; R = Representative. Missing months may be estimated.
stations.history: Airport history metadata reaches 1931; supplied GHCNd daily elements begin in May 1998. NOAA temperature normal is Representative, with estimated missing months.

stations.name: Long Beach airport · coastal plain
stations.quality: NOAA variable-specific flags: High (TMAX): S, 24–26 available years; Low (TMIN): R, 22–23 available years; Mean (TAVG): R, 22–23 available years; Rain: S, 29–30 years. S = Standard; R = Representative. Missing months may be estimated.
stations.history: Airport metadata reaches 1930; supplied daily elements begin January 1949. Coastal-plain airport is inland from the waterfront.

historical.title: The wet years and the dry ones
historical.text: Complete GHCNd calendar-year rain sums at LAX include about 27.1 inches in 1998, 3.6 in 2013 and 25.4 in 2023. Those are specific observed years, not future odds. Compare the full 35-year record below.

historical.title: A long dry season
historical.text: LAX’s rounded monthly normals sum to 12.23 inches annually; approximately 87% is in November–March. Downtown’s sum is 14.25 inches. Year-to-year totals and timing vary substantially.

historical.title: A warmer California
historical.text: NOAA’s 2022 state assessment reports nearly 3°F of statewide warming since the early twentieth century. It reports large precipitation variability. This is regional context; we have not estimated an El Segundo warming rate.

historical.title: Keep the plan adaptable
historical.text: The same assessment’s future warming and drought discussion depends on emissions pathways and model assumptions. This atlas uses that as a reason to keep shade, water and indoor alternatives in the plan; no future local values are forecast here.

mapping.title: A weather day, plotted
mapping.text: Beginning in 1871, daily weather maps assembled station readings into a wider pattern: pressure, rain and temperature. They help place an unusual day in context. A 2000 NWS regional guide plotted local reference stations and illustrated an August 1999 inversion.
mapping.limit: A dated synoptic map describes that observation time. It is not a neighborhood comfort map or an event-frequency estimate.

mapping.title: The landscape underneath
mapping.text: USGS historic topographic maps (printed editions 1884–2006) supply contours, waterways and settlement. Hills, slope and ocean exposure help interpret why nearby stations differ. Compare dated editions carefully.
mapping.limit: Contours show elevation. Historic maps need their edition, datum and georeferencing before an overlay; we did not digitize a local historic sheet here.

mapping.title: A model between stations
mapping.text: Modern PRISM normals estimate a climate surface using observations, elevation and other physical relationships. Its current 1991–2020 products have 800 m and 4 km grids. A seasonal suitability map then adds a clearly labeled purpose.
mapping.limit: No PRISM cells are shown here. Current map zones are illustrative terrain classes, not interpolated observations. A quantitative next edition requires documented processing and validation.

dailyExtraction.annualRule: report rain total only when every expected calendar day has an accepted precipitation value
